newsitem.title: INDIA: India cable group appeals Time Warner ruling.
newsitem.headline: India cable group appeals Time Warner ruling.

text.p: India's IndusIndia Media and Communications, a Hinduja Group subsidiary, said on Tuesday it filed an appeal against a restraint order imposed by a local court in a trade-mark lawsuit filed by Time Warner Inc.

"We have taken objection to the observations of the judge as well as the restraining order passed by him. Our appeal will be heard on June 6," Ashok Mansukhani, the CEO of IndusInd Media and Communications (IIMC) told Reuters.
Time Warner launched the suit in the Delhi High Court in September 1996 when IIMC started promoting a Hindi film-based entertainment channel under the name of "Cable Box Office" or "CBO".

Time Warner said CBO was too close to the name of its HBO (Home Box Office) movie channel. On Monday a Delhi High Court judge handed down an interim injunction restraining IIMC from using the CBO label and sent the dispute to trial.

HBO is not a registered trade mark in India. Time Warner applied to register the name in 1994, HBO's associate counsel Noreen Weiss told Reuters by telephone from New York. The application is pending with Indian authorities.

She said Time Warner would likely seek damages, adding that the U.S. news and entertainment conglomerate would continue to press its right to its trademark in India. She refused to put a figure to the damages Time Warner might seek.
